question.prompt: If \(\log_2(\log_2(\log_2(x)))=2,\) then how many digits are in the base-ten representation for \(x?\)

solutions.explanation:
The definition \(\log_2 u=v\) means \(u=2^v\). Apply this definition to the outermost logarithm first, then repeat:
\[
\log_2(\log_2 x)=2^2=4,
\]
\[
\log_2 x=2^4=16,
\]
\[
x=2^{16}=65536.
\]
The logarithm arguments at this value are \(65536\), \(16\), and \(4\), all positive, so every logarithm is defined. The number \(65536\) has \(\boxed{5}\) decimal digits, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutions.title: Undo the logarithms from outside inward
